To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the critical exponents in a class of twist map models and in the FK models are all determined by the degree of inflection of the nonanalytic potential function.
the degree of inflection of the external potential in a twist map or FK model plays the same role as dimensionality in phase transition theory.
the degree of inflection of a nonanalytic external potential is a new parameter that controls the scaling behavior of invariant curves and that it plays the role of a dimensionality for the FK model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a class of twist map models in which the nonanalyticity of the external potential function plays a role similar to that of dimensionality.
the study of the effects of a variable degree of singularity of the potential on the dynamics of the twist map and the FK model.
the scaling properties of invariant curves and the pinning-depinng transition in the FK model, with a special focus on the role of the degree of inflection in the external potential.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nonanalyticity of the external potential function plays a role similar to that of dimensionality, and that the critical exponents and scaling behaviors are the same as those of a standard FK model when the degree of inflection is greater than three.
the critical exponents are independent of the degree of nonanalyticity of the external potential when z ⩾3, while the scaling behavior is dependent of the degree of inflection when z < 3.
, in the presence of nonanalytic external potential, the FK model exhibits a sequence of transitions with critical exponents dependent on z, and with z = 3 as the upper critical dimension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonanalyticity of the external potential function in the FK model is a key factor in determining its phase diagram.

the nonanalyticity and the degree of inflection are the key parameters that govern the recurrence of the invariant curve, the scaling behaviors of the invariant curves, the pinning-depinping transitions, and the phonon gap.
a nonanalytic external potential with a variable degree z of inflection is equivalent to a variable number of dimensions in the FK model, and the critical behavior of both systems is controlled by z.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the critical behavior of the FK model is governed not by the dimensionality of the system, but by the degree of inflection of the external potential.
a nonanalytic twist map or FK model is a very rich system in which a variety of phenomena are observed.
nonanalyticity is not a mere technicality but a fundamental ingredient in the physics of these models.
